description:
The Preservation of Tiatr Literature scheme was launched by the Government of Goa in 2021.

This initiative aims to preserve and promote the rich cultural heritage of Tiatr, which is a form of musical theater that originated in Goa.

Tiatr has a significant historical context as it has been performed in Goa since the late 19th century.

The art form reflects the socio-political issues faced by Goans and is performed in the Konkani language.

The scheme was introduced to address the decline in the production of Tiatr literature and to support playwrights and artists.

One of the main objectives of the scheme is to document and archive existing Tiatr scripts and performances.

The government aims to create a comprehensive database of Tiatr literature by the end of 2023.

This database will include scripts, recordings, and other relevant materials related to Tiatr.

Another objective is to provide financial assistance to playwrights for the creation of new Tiatr scripts.

The scheme allocates a budget of INR 1 crore for the preservation and promotion of Tiatr literature over a span of five years.

The financial assistance provided to playwrights can be up to INR 50,000 per script.

This assistance is aimed at encouraging new talent and reviving interest in Tiatr among the younger generation.

Eligibility for financial assistance under this scheme is open to individuals who are recognized playwrights in the Tiatr community.

Applicants must have a minimum of three completed Tiatr scripts to qualify for the financial assistance.

Additionally, applicants must be residents of Goa and must be above the age of 18 years.

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability.

Interested playwrights must submit an application form along with a copy of their completed scripts.

They are also required to provide proof of residency in Goa and any relevant documentation that establishes their credentials as playwrights.

The applications are reviewed by a committee formed by the Department of Art and Culture of Goa.

This committee consists of experienced members from the Tiatr community and experts in the field of performing arts.

Once the applications are approved, the financial assistance is disbursed within 30 days.

The scheme also includes provisions for organizing workshops and seminars to promote Tiatr literature.

These workshops aim to educate new playwrights about the nuances of writing for Tiatr.

The government plans to conduct at least four workshops annually.

Each workshop will accommodate around 30 participants to ensure personalized attention.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of digital archiving of Tiatr performances.

The government intends to collaborate with local universities and cultural organizations to digitize Tiatr performances.

This digitization process is expected to begin in early 2024.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Art and Culture of the Government of Goa.

They are responsible for overseeing the implementation and monitoring of the scheme.

Contact details for the Department of Art and Culture can be found on the official Goa government website.

The scheme also aims to foster collaborations between Tiatr artists and educational institutions.

This collaboration will help in integrating Tiatr literature into academic curricula.

The government envisions that this will enhance the appreciation of Tiatr among students.

Moreover, the scheme encourages the participation of local communities in Tiatr performances.

Community engagement is seen as a vital aspect of preserving this cultural heritage.

The government has also planned to organize an annual Tiatr festival.

This festival will showcase new works and celebrate the contributions of established playwrights.

The first Tiatr festival under this scheme is scheduled for December 2023.

The festival aims to attract audiences from all over Goa and beyond.

It will feature performances, workshops, and discussions on the future of Tiatr literature.

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme provides mentorship opportunities for emerging playwrights.

Mentorship will be offered by established figures in the Tiatr community.

This initiative is designed to ensure the continuity of Tiatr literature and its evolution.

The government has set a target of supporting at least 100 new Tiatr scripts by 2025.

This target is part of a broader strategy to revitalize the Tiatr art form.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of preserving the historical context of Tiatr.

Historical records and scripts will be collected and preserved in collaboration with local libraries.

The government aims to create a repository of Tiatr literature that can be accessed by researchers and enthusiasts.

This repository is expected to be launched by mid-2024.

The scheme recognizes the role of Tiatr in promoting social issues and cultural identity.

It encourages playwrights to address contemporary issues through their works.

The government believes that Tiatr can serve as a powerful medium for social change.

By supporting Tiatr literature, the government aims to strengthen the cultural fabric of Goa.

The scheme is part of a larger initiative to promote the arts and culture sector in the state.

Overall, the Preservation of Tiatr Literature scheme represents a significant step towards safeguarding an important aspect of Goan heritage.

It provides concrete support to artists and playwrights while fostering community engagement.

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the preservation and promotion of Tiatr literature in Goa.
